extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors submitting papers to ICML 2025 (machine learning researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and policies for preparing and submitting research (and position) papers to the ICML 2025 main conference, including formatting, review, ethics, and author responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper length and file format
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers must be prepared and submitted as a single file: 8 pages for the main paper, with unlimited pages for references, the impact statement, and appendices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final versions of accepted papers will be allowed one extra page for the main paper. Submitted papers that do not conform to these policies will be rejected without review. There will be no separate deadline for the submission of supplementary material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines are strict
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract and paper submission deadlines are strict. In no circumstances will extensions be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission site open: January 9, 2025; suggested OpenReview account creation deadline; abstract submission deadline and full paper submission deadline given with AoE times. Abstract and paper deadlines are enforced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract, title, and authorship change policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should include a full title for their paper, complete author list, and complete abstract in the submission form by the abstract submission deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title and abstract can be edited until the full paper submission deadline, but submissions with 'placeholder' abstracts that are substantially rewritten for the full submission risk being removed without consideration. The author list cannot be changed after the abstract deadline. After the abstract deadline, authors may be reordered, but additions or removals must be justified in writing and approved on a case-by-case basis by the program chairs; approval only in exceptional circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: OpenReview account requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors must have an OpenReview account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is strongly recommended to sign up with an institutional email; institutional email activates immediately, otherwise activation can take up to 2 weeks. If you do not already have an OpenReview account, register by the suggested account-creation deadline or activation may not occur in time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal reviewing requirement (author reviewing obligation)
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions must have at least one author who agrees to serve as a reviewer for ICML; every author with 4 or more submissions must agree to serve as a reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The designated author should be qualified to review according to the Peer Review FAQ. If none of the authors are qualified, or if all qualified authors are serving as SACs/ACs/organizers, the submission is exempt. The abstract submission form allows designating an author or indicating exemption. Submissions that do not meet this requirement may be desk rejected. Reviewers who fail to adequately participate (e.g., not submitting reviews on time or submitting highly insufficient/inappropriate reviews) may have their own submissions desk rejected. The reciprocal reviewing requirement does not apply to the position paper track.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind review and anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: All papers will be reviewed in a double-blind process and all submissions must be anonymized and may not contain information intended or resulting in violating double-blind reviewing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may post versions on preprint servers (e.g., arXiv) and give talks during review, but must not advertise the work as an ICML submission during the review period. If a non-anonymized version is posted online before decisions are made, the submitted (anonymized) version must not refer to the non-anonymized version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual submission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may not submit papers that are identical, or substantially similar, to versions previously published, accepted, or submitted in parallel to other conferences or journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizers may reject or remove such submissions. Concurrent ICML submissions with overlapping authors are treated as prior work (e.g., if publishing one would render the other too incremental). Submissions presented at workshops without published proceedings do not violate this policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing criteria for acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions should report original and rigorous research of significant interest to the machine learning community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All claims must be clearly stated and supported by reproducible experiments and/or sound theoretical analysis. Contributions must be situated in the broader literature and differentiated from relevant prior work. See reviewer instructions for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of generative AI in papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are allowed to use generative AI tools (e.g., LLMs) to assist in writing or research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must take full responsibility for all content, including AI-generated content that might be construed as plagiarism or scientific misconduct. Authors are encouraged to explain any notable ways these tools were used in their research methodology. LLMs are not eligible for authorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical conduct requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are expected to follow standard ethical conduct for peer review and research dissemination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plagiarism in any form is forbidden. Advertising work as under submission to ICML during the review period is forbidden. Any form of collusion with reviewers, ACs, or SACs is forbidden. Suspected unethical behavior should be reported via the Ethics Violation Reporting form; violations will be investigated and may lead to sanctions or rejection, and names of violators may be collected and shared with other organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact statement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are required to include a statement of the potential broader impact of their work, including ethical aspects and future societal consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statement must be a separate section at the end of the paper (co-located with Acknowledgements, before References) and does not count toward the page limit. In many cases a brief standard statement is acceptable, but authors are encouraged to provide further discussion when warranted. Reviewers and ACs may flag submissions for ethics review; ethics reviewers provide comments but cannot reject—however, program chairs may reject papers on ethical grounds in extreme cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lay summaries for accepted papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors of accepted papers will be required to submit a short 'lay summary' (plain language summary) when submitting camera-ready materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is new for the year; further details and examples will be provided prior to the camera-ready deadline. The purpose is to improve science communication to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attendance/presentation requirement for accepted papers
rubrics_metrics.description: At least one of the authors of accepted papers must attend the conference in person to present the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is required except in exceptional circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position paper track separate policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Position paper submissions are handled separately from research paper submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Position papers have a separate Call for Position Papers and separate OpenReview site. The reciprocal reviewing requirement does not apply to position paper submissions this year. Impact statements are optional for the position paper track.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for nonconformance and misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions not conforming to ICML policies or engaging in prohibited conduct may face rejection or other sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: nonconforming submissions will be rejected without review; failure to meet reciprocal review requirement may cause desk rejection; unethical conduct will be investigated with possible sanctions and sharing of names of violators with other organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission site and timing details
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers and abstracts must be submitted via the specified OpenReview group for ICML 2025, with explicit open and deadline dates (including AoE timezone specifications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested OpenReview account creation deadline and link provided. Abstract submission and full paper submission deadlines include AoE timestamps; position papers use a separate OpenReview site.
